findings.heading: ### The **reprex** package
findings.proposition: The English says reprex ships with tidyverse so loading EITHER package suffices; the Turkish says you must load BOTH packages ("her iki paketi de yüklemelisiniz").
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader believes a separate library(reprex) call is mandatory alongside tidyverse, and may conclude their setup is broken when the code chunk below loads only tidyverse.

findings.heading: ## Github issues
findings.proposition: The English link points the reader to the Collaboration and Github chapter at target collaboration.qmd; the Turkish keeps the label but drops the link target entirely, leaving bare text [İşbirliği ve Github].
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot reach the Collaboration and Github chapter; the text renders as literal square brackets with no hyperlink, so the pointer to how to store work on Github is lost.

findings.heading: ## Resources
findings.proposition: The English URL fragment is #producing-a-minimal-dataset; the Turkish URL fragment is #production-a-minimal-dataset, an anchor that does not exist on the target page.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader following the minimal-dataset tips link lands at the top of the external page instead of the relevant section, and may not find the guidance at all.

findings.heading: ## Resources
findings.proposition: The English provides a working markdown link whose label "get help!" is attached to the tidyverse help URL; in the Turkish the label [yardım alacağınız] is separated from the URL by the words "hakkında Tidyverse sayfası!", so no hyperlink is produced.
findings.reader_consequence: The tidyverse help resource is not clickable for the Turkish reader; the page shows stray brackets and a raw URL, and the first Resources entry stops working.

findings.heading: ### The **reprex** package
findings.proposition: The English says session_info = TRUE includes your R version AND your R package versions; the Turkish names only package versions ("R paket sürümlerinize").
findings.reader_consequence: The reader does not learn that the R version itself is reported, so they may add it manually or omit it when helpers ask which R version they run.

findings.heading: ## Posting to a forum
findings.proposition: The English qualifies the answer as one that meets the ORIGINAL request; the Turkish drops "original" and says only "isteği karşılayan bir yanıt" (an answer that meets the request).
findings.reader_consequence: The reader loses the instruction to judge the answer against the question as first asked, and may mark a thread answered for a later, shifted version of the question.
